facts.text: TANK says all of its buses are accessible to riders using wheelchairs or other mobility devices, with either a ramp or a lift for wheelchair boarding plus a kneeling feature; riders who walk can also ask for the ramp, lift or kneeling feature.
quote: All TANK buses are accessible to individuals with disabilities including passengers using wheelchairs or other mobility devices. TANK’s buses are equipped with either “ramps” or “lifts” for wheelchair boarding and “kneeling devices” for general boarding. Ambulatory passengers can also request use of the ramp, lift or kneeling device to make boarding easier.

facts.text: On fixed routes, TANK announces transfer points, major intersections, destinations and other points along the route, either electronically or by the operator over the PA system.
quote: On fixed route service, TANK announces all transfer points, major intersections, destination points and other intervals along a route to permit individuals with visual impairments or other disabilities to be oriented to their location. These announcements may be made electronically or be made by the bus operator over the PA system.

facts.text: Riders may bring a respirator, concentrator or portable oxygen if the device is free of cracks, leaks, dents, gouges or pits; the operator may inspect it, and it must be secured so it does not move while the bus is in motion.
quote: Passengers who use a respirator, concentrator or portable oxygen are permitted to ride all TANK buses as long as the device is free of cracks, leaks, dents, gouges or pits. These devices are subject to inspection by the bus operator and must be secured in such a way that the device does not move when the bus is in motion.

facts.text: RAMP is TANK’s door-to-door paratransit service for people unable to use its fixed-route buses. The eligibility page describes service in areas of Boone, Campbell and Kenton counties that are also served by TANK’s fixed-route system; this does not establish that every address in those counties is covered.
quote: The Regional Area Mobility Program (RAMP) is a door to door paratransit service available to disabled citizens who are unable to use TANK’s fixed route bus service. RAMP serves the areas of Boone, Campbell, and Kenton counties in Northern Kentucky, which are also served by TANK’s fixed route system.

facts.text: TANK’s eligibility page tells applicants to request a RAMP application at 859-814-2135, obtain a doctor’s medical verification and then schedule an assessment; it also offers large-print or recorded schedules on request.
quote: Large print and or recorded schedules are available upon request. qualifying for ramp services Please call our Special Services office at 859-814-2135 to receive information on program eligibility and registration, reserving your rides, planning your trip, fares, passenger assistance, cancellations, transfers and other policies you need to know in order to use RAMP. Steps to qualify to use RAMP Request Application 859-814-2135 Medical Verification filled out by Doctor Call to set up assessment upon completing the first 2 steps above

facts.text: Reduced fares are for riders 65+ and people with disabilities (proof of Medicare or SSI). Get a TANK Reduced Fare Photo ID at headquarters, or show a Medicare card with photo ID.
quote: TANK offers a reduced fare for senior citizens (age 65 and over) and for people with disabilities (proof of Medicare or SSI assistance is required to receive the discount.) Eligible persons should have a TANK Reduced Fare Photo ID made at the TANK headquarters to show the driver. A Medicare card may also be presented, with valid photo ID.

facts.text: Ask the driver when you board and they will call out any stop.
quote: Drivers will also call out any stop upon request, if you ask when you get on the bus.

facts.text: TANK says riders with disabilities are given ample time to board and get off safely.
quote: Ample time will be provided to passengers with disabilities to board and disembark in a safe manner.

facts.text: TANK says riders do not need to show service-animal certification, but may be asked whether the animal is required because of a disability and what work it is trained to perform. It must remain under its owner’s control and not pose a direct threat to others. Reasonable-modification requests can be made by phone, in person or online.
quote: Service animals are permitted to accompany individuals with disabilities on all TANK buses. A service animal is any guide dog or other animal trained to work or perform tasks for an individual with a disability. Passengers are not required to show proof of service animal certification but may be asked if the service animal is required because of a disability and/or what work the service animal has been trained to perform. A service animal must be under the control of its owner at all times and cannot pose a direct threat to the health or safety of others. Respirators, Concentrators or Portable Oxygen Passengers who use a respirator, concentrator or portable oxygen are permitted to ride all TANK buses as long as the device is free of cracks, leaks, dents, gouges or pits. These devices are subject to inspection by the bus operator and must be secured in such a way that the device does not move when the bus is in motion. modifications for persons with disabilities Reduced Fares for Persons with Disabilities Reduced fares are available to individuals with disabilities by obtaining a Reduced Fare Card with a photo identification. TANK offers a reduced fare for senior citizens (age 65 and over) and for people with disabilities (proof of Medicare or SSI assistance is required to receive the discount.) Eligible persons should have a TANK Reduced Fare Photo ID made at the TANK headquarters to show the driver. A Medicare card may also be presented, with valid photo ID. Once qualified, a passenger with a Reduced Fare Card must present the card to the bus operator when boarding for a reduced fare. Requests for Reasonable Modifications A request for reasonable modification to TANK’s policies or practices can be made by contacting TANK by phone, in person or on-line using the following resources:

facts.text: Having a disability does not by itself qualify you for RAMP. A bench or shelter for a stop can be requested through the TANK service request form.
quote: How can I request a shelter or bench at a bus stop? To request transit amenities for your bus stop, you can fill out the TANK service request form. Our Transit Planner will then research the relevant stop(s) to determine whether it is eligible for amenities. You can visit the TANK Service Request Form here . How can I share my ideas on improving TANK? TANK loves all input it receives from members of the Northern Kentucky community. Your input, whether positive and negative, is vital to ensuring that TANK is meeting its goals of providing accessible, meaningful transportation to the public. You can provide your ideas for improvement through email, phone, or text on the TANK Customer Service page . Alternatively, you can fill out two forms to provide feedback or request TANK services or amenities in your area. RAMP Paratransit What is paratransit? Is it different from regular TANK service? Paratransit is a form of transportation that provides door-to-door transportation for individuals across Boone, Campbell, and Kenton Counties. Rather than operating from a fixed set of bus stops, TANK RAMP vehicles, which are smaller than a traditional bus, pick up individuals at their doors. TANK is committed to ensuring that those with functional limitations can have equitable participation and access to the Northern Kentucky community and its resources. How do I know if I am qualified for RAMP paratransit? RAMP Paratransit is an ADA service designed to serve those individuals with functional limitations—including visual, physical, and mental limitations—preventing them from accessing or using TANK bus stops/fixed route service. Having a disability does not necessarily qualify you for the RAMP program. To determine whether you qualify for this service, you can call the TANK special service office at (859)-814-2135. From there, you will work with your doctor to set up an assessment and complete the RAMP application.

facts.text: TANK asks riders to leave the front seats for older passengers and riders with disabilities, and to keep the aisles clear.
quote: Keep aisles clear, strollers must be folded. Do not stand in front of the standee line. Do not open windows while climate control systems are in operation. Leave front seats open for older passengers and riders with disabilities.

facts.text: The passenger signal cord runs across the middle of the bus windows. TANK asks riders to pull it about one block before the stop they want.
quote: All TANK buses are equipped with a passenger signal cord. The cord is located across the middle of the windows. Please pull the signal cord to request your bus stop about one block before the stop you wish to use.

facts.text: TANK offers one-to-one travel training, usually on the route the rider would use; the rider’s needs determine when and where it happens. Training has no charge, but standard bus fares still apply.
quote: Your needs will determine when and where Travel Training is held. We offer day classes to work with your schedule. Training is usually held on the particular route you would use. Types of Training Trip Training Participants in this type of training work one-on-one with a Travel Trainer to practiced using buses to travel to locations they visit on a regular basis. During Trip Training sessions, participants will learn how to recognize landmarks to know when to get off the bus and how to interact with transit personnel and other riders. Individual Orientation Participants in this type of training will work one-on-one with a Travel Trainer to receive a general introduction to bus accessibility. The goal of Individual Transit Orientation is to educate participants on how to use the entire transit system. During Individual Transit Orientation sessions, a Travel Trainer will explain how to use accessibility features in transit vehicles and how to plan trips on TANK. In addition, Travel Trainers may take participants to a bus garage to practice boarding transit vehicles or practice using buses to build confidence. Group Transit Orientation This type of training provides group presentations at agencies that serve people with disabilities and older adults throughout the three county regions. The goal of Group Transit Orientation is to give participants and agency staff an introduction to the accessibility of TANK, and to demonstrate the benefits of using fixed route buses. During Group Transit Orientation presentations, a Travel Trainer will explain how to use accessibility features in transit vehicles, how to plan trips, pay fares on TANK and how to travel safely in the community while using buses. What does Travel Training involve? Planning your trip Riding specific routes Reading and understanding route maps and schedules Learning how to get to and from your bus stop Understanding the fare structure and how to purchase fare medium Getting on and off the bus safely Transferring to other buses Street crossing Stranger awareness Safety skills Learning to travel independently and with confidence on the bus Is there a cost for Travel Training? There is no charge for Travel Training, but the standard bus fares do apply when riding the bus.

facts.text: TANK Plus is curb-to-curb service within its designated zone, or a connection to a listed fixed-route transfer point. The driver does not pull into driveways; riders meet it at the end of a driveway or at a designated location.
quote: What is TANK Plus? TANK Plus is a flexible, on-demand way to get around town, curb-to-curb within our designated zones…or connecting you to our fixed route service to travel outside of the zones. Instead of fixed bus routes, we use smaller vehicles that you can schedule when you need a ride, either through the TANK+ app or our call center. It’s all about making your transit experience more personalized and convenient. *Please note, curb-to-curb means you would need to walk to the end of your driveway or a designated location to be picked up. The driver will not pull into driveways.

facts.text: For TANK Plus, select wheelchair use in the app when booking, or notify the driver at pickup. TANK says each Plus vehicle has space for three wheelchairs.
quote: Are vehicles accessible to people with wheelchairs? Yes, you can select wheelchair in the app when booking, or notify the driver at pick up. Each TANK Plus vehicle has space for three wheelchairs.

facts.text: TANK Plus bookings are for an immediate trip, not a future day or time. Use the TANK+ app or call 859-331-8265. The agency suggests requesting a ride about 20–30 minutes before it is needed; availability is limited.
quote: TANK Plus trips can also be scheduled by calling 859-331-8265. TANK Plus is like ride share; you cannot book for an advanced day/time. Booking TANK Plus is for an immediate trip. We suggest booking about 20-30 minutes before you need to be picked up/dropped off. You can schedule a ride with TANK Plus through the app or by calling 859-331-8265, and the designated vehicle will pick you up within 30 minutes and drop you off, curb-to-curb. If the pick-up time is greater than 30 minutes, you will receive a message to try again later.

facts.text: Packages can be carried on TANK Plus, but may not occupy a seat. Operators are not permitted to help passengers with packages.
quote: If I go shopping, can I bring my packages on TANK Plus? Yes, you may bring packages on board TANK Plus vehicles; however, packages may not take up a seat and operators are not permitted to assist customers with packages.

facts.text: Covington Transit Center is one of the listed TANK Plus fixed-route transfer points. A Plus connection costs $2.50 each way, with a separate full fare for the fixed-route trip; regular TANK passes and reduced-fare cards are not accepted on Plus. Confirm the requested journey is in the service zone.
quote: Fare Information: Traveling curb-to-curb within the zone is $5.00 per trip Traveling from your zone to a designated fixed route transfer point is $2.50 per trip (Full bus fare will apply for fixed route trips) Fixed Route Transfer Points: Covington Transit Center Monmouth @ Carothers Bus Stop St. Elizabeth-Ft. Thomas Bus Stop Lakeside Dorms NKU Bus Stop NKU Student Union Island Drop Off/Pick Up Points: An “Island” is a drop off or pick up only destination. How To Book Your Trip Booking a ride is simple with the TANK+ app. You can download our app for free on any smart phone device with location services enabled. TANK Plus trips can also be scheduled by calling 859-331-8265. TANK Plus is like ride share; you cannot book for an advanced day/time. Booking TANK Plus is for an immediate trip. We suggest booking about 20-30 minutes before you need to be picked up/dropped off. You can schedule a ride with TANK Plus through the app or by calling 859-331-8265, and the designated vehicle will pick you up within 30 minutes and drop you off, curb-to-curb. If the pick-up time is greater than 30 minutes, you will receive a message to try again later. You do not need to be at a fixed route bus stop to ride TANK Plus. Zone Info FAQ What is TANK Plus? TANK Plus is a flexible, on-demand way to get around town, curb-to-curb within our designated zones…or connecting you to our fixed route service to travel outside of the zones. Instead of fixed bus routes, we use smaller vehicles that you can schedule when you need a ride, either through the TANK+ app or our call center. It’s all about making your transit experience more personalized and convenient. *Please note, curb-to-curb means you would need to walk to the end of your driveway or a designated location to be picked up. The driver will not pull into driveways. When will TANK Plus start? TANK Plus launched August 13th, 2024. When is the last time I can schedule a ride on TANK Plus? Ride scheduling is available until 5:59PM on weekdays and 4:59PM on Saturday’s; however, ride availability is determined on a first come, first served basis. Can I ride TANK Plus anywhere I need to go? TANK Plus can transport passengers within their zone(s) or connect passengers to fixed route transfer points to travel outside of the zone. TANK Plus zones are as follows: Zone 1 | Campbell County How do I know where to meet my driver? Passengers will establish a pickup location when scheduling a trip on the TANK+ app or over the phone during the booking process. TANK Plus will pick up passengers, curb-to-curb, at the location requested when scheduling a ride. Customers using the TANK+ app will be able to track the vehicle on a map in the app (similar to Uber). What is the fare? The TANK Plus fare is $5.00 each way for each passenger. If you are connecting to a transfer point from TANK Plus to fixed route service, the fare will cost $2.50 for each trip. You can use the TANK+ app and pay by credit card/debit card or you can pay cash when you board. If I transfer to TANK Plus from a regular TANK route, do I have to pay the $2.50 fare? Yes, TANK Plus is an on-demand service. You will have to schedule a ride with Tank Plus from one of the designated fixed route transfer point locations to travel. Fixed Route transfer point locations: Covington Transit Center Monmouth @ Carothers Bus Stop St. Elizabeth-Ft. Thomas Bus Stop Lakeside Dorms NKU Bus Stop NKU Student Union What is an Island Drop Off/Pick Up Point? An “Island” is a drop off or pick up only destination. The zone does not expand to cover the surrounding areas near these Islands. The cost to or from an Island is $5.00 per trip. + Saratoga Place Apartments in Newport + Two Rivers Apartments in Newport + Campbell County Public Library, Newport Branch + Watertower Square Building in Newport + 103 Landmark Ave. in Bellevue What if I have one or more passengers with me? You may schedule a ride for up to four riders for each trip (yourself + 3 others). The passenger scheduling will pay the total fare price. Will regular TANK passes be accepted by TANK Plus? No, TANK Plus is a premium service with specialized scheduling, so regular TANK passes will not be accepted. Will TANK Plus accept discount offers, like the reduced fare card/sticker? No, TANK Plus is a premium service and will not accept any discount offers or other discount program cards.

facts.text: TANK’s service-change notice effective November 7, 2026 says the Southbank Shuttle and Route 16 are replaced by a corridor served by fixed-route buses. It directs former Route 16 riders to the new Route 1 and Licking River Link; use current schedules when planning a journey.
quote: Service Improvements Go into Effect Nov. 7, 2026 The changes reflect rider and community feedback and will deliver more reliable trips, more frequent service on key routes, better regional connections and support long-term sustainable operations. What’s changing? Starting Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026, riders will see the following service improvements: Route 1 will be extended to Newport with service ending at St. Elizabeth Healthcare in Ft. Thomas and will operate as a standalone service (no longer interlined with Route 25). Routes 3, 7 and 12 peak frequencies will increase to every 30 minutes Southbank Shuttle and Route 16 will be replaced with a new high-frequency corridor connecting downtown Newport, Covington and downtown Cincinnati with service provided by a fixed-route bus. Service will operate every 7-8 minutes along the areas currently served by Route 1, interlined Routes 3/12 and interlined Routes 7/25, and every 15 minutes along areas served by Route 1 and interlined Routes 7/25. Riders who currently use Route 16 will have access to the new Route 1 and the Licking River Link as alternative service options.

facts.text: Senior Transportation accepts medical appointments, essential trips such as grocery or pharmacy visits, and facility trips such as senior centers. facts.text: Book Senior Transportation by calling 859-578-6949, Monday–Friday 10 a.m.–5 p.m., up to one week ahead. TANK provides a 30-minute pickup window rather than an exact pickup time. Booking-office hours differ from the program’s travel hours.
quote: Trips can be scheduled by calling 859-578-6949 between 10 a.m. and 5 p.m. Monday-Friday. Trips can be scheduled up to one week in advance. A 30-minute pick-up window will be provided.

facts.text: RAMP’s service-area page distinguishes a red area described as the required ADA area ($2.50) from a green area outside it ($5). Call 859-814-2135 to check both addresses; the colours and fares do not mean every Northern Kentucky address is served. The page dates the two-zone arrangement to January 2021.
quote: Beginning in January 2021, the RAMP Service area has been separated into two zones based on the ADA required area.
Inside Strict ADA Area (red): $2.50 Outside Required ADA Area (green) : $5
If you are unsure if your origin or destination is inside the strict ADA area, please contact the RAMP office at 859-814-2135

facts.text: The regional paratransit application says Northern Kentucky applicants must attend an in-person assessment, with transport to it provided by the local transit provider. Bring valid photo ID and any mobility device you use; call 859-814-2135 to schedule and submit the application.
quote: If you live in Hamilton County, Ohio, or Northern Kentucky, you will be required to complete an in-person assessment. Transportation to the assessment location will be provided by your local transit provider. You must bring a valid photo identification card and if you utilize a mobility device, you must bring it as well to your in-person assessment.
Northern Kentucky residents o Call (859) 814-2135 to schedule an assessment and submit your application.

facts.text: The regional paratransit application offers help completing the form and alternative formats, including large print or a different language. It says all sections must be completed.
quote: If you have questions, need help filling out this application, or need an alternative format (large print or in a different language), we can help you. All sections must be completed.

facts.text: The regional application says applicants may be asked for a clinical professional’s assessment form. Confirm which paperwork is needed for your application.
quote: You may be asked to have a clinical professional complete an assessment form for you.

facts.text: The regional application describes a written decision within 21 days after the assessment is completed. It says the decision letter identifies any eligibility conditions and whether a personal care attendant is approved for travel; approval should not be assumed before that decision.
quote: All applications for ADA paratransit service eligibility will be processed within 21 days from the date that the assessment is completed. Staff will notify the applicant in writing of the determination decision. The letter will state if the applicant has been approved for service, the conditions of eligibility (if any) and if a Personal Care Attendant (PCA) is approved for travel as well.

facts.text: TANK Plus permits a booking for up to four people in total, including the person booking. That person pays the total fare; this is a Plus group-booking rule, not a RAMP attendant entitlement.
quote: You may schedule a ride for up to four riders for each trip (yourself + 3 others). The passenger scheduling will pay the total fare price.

facts.text: TANK’s alert dated October 29, 2026 temporarily removes the Route 39X stop at Petersburg and Elijah Creek because of road work. It gives no completion or reinstatement date; check current alerts before using that stop.
quote: Petersburg at Elijah Creek Stop Closure EFFECTIVE DATE: 10/29/2026 The stop at Petersburg at Elijah Creek on 39X has been temporarily removed due to some road work in that area. We do not have a date for when the work will be done or when we can reinstall it.

facts.text: Jungle Jim’s says motorized shopping carts and traditional wheelchairs are available at the main entrances of both stores, including Eastgate. It does not publish availability guarantees, fit limits or a reservation procedure.
quote: Motorized shopping carts and traditional wheelchairs are available at the main entrances at both locations.

facts.text: A Caroline Cart can be requested at Customer Service. The FAQ does not describe its collection route, fit limits or transfer assistance.
quote: A Caroline Cart is available by special request at Customer Service.

facts.text: The Eastgate store is at 4450 Eastgate South Drive, Cincinnati, OH 45245, with free parking in the store lot. Designated-space locations and the parking-to-door route are not described.
quote: 4450 Eastgate South Drive Cincinnati, OH 45245 513-674-6000 Free parking in store lot

facts.text: The operator describes Eastgate as having wider aisles and brighter lighting, with themed displays including the Hot Sauce Drone and Candy Castle. These are the operator’s descriptions, not measured clearances or lighting levels.
quote: Established in 2012, our Eastgate location enjoys wider aisles, brighter lighting, and an easier to shop layout. It's bursting with fun displays like the high-flying Hot Sauce Drone and killer departments like the Candy Castle and one of Ohio's largest liquor stores.

facts.text: The FAQ says regular in-store merchandise cannot currently be ordered online for pickup or delivery. Limited online offers are separate; party trays are for in-store pickup at Fairfield, not Eastgate.
quote: We are not offering online ordering, pick up, or delivery for our regular in-store merchandise at this time.
We currently have limited online ordering for event tickets, party trays, Cooking School certificates, and gift cards.
Party trays are only available for in-store pickup at the Fairfield location.

facts.text: Guided store tours require advance reservations, run Monday–Friday subject to availability, and have limited availability during holidays and December. For Eastgate tours, contact 513-674-6033 or tours-eg@junglejims.com.
quote: Advance reservations required for all tours.
Tours are available Monday-Friday only.
Limited tour availability during holidays and the month of December.
Tour dates and times are subject to availability.
Eastgate Reservations tours-eg@junglejims.com 513-674-6033

facts.text: Store Safari Tours last about an hour and involve substantial walking. The operator says tours can be tailored to special requirements for groups of eight or more; smaller groups can often be paired with others. Confirm rest opportunities and equipment needs when reserving.
quote: Tours can be tailored to meet special requirements, interests, and to fit groups of 8 or more (smaller groups can often be paired with others).
Comfortable shoes are suggested, as a good deal of walking is involved.
Store Tours last approximately one hour

facts.text: The guided Store Safari Tour includes a guide using a microphone. The page does not describe assistive-listening equipment, captioning or a quiet-tour option.
quote: Tour Guide w/ microphone.

facts.text: The chain’s pet policy allows service animals and excludes pets.
quote: No pets – service animals only.

facts.text: The trip-planning page links a printable Eastgate store map and describes an interactive map in the Jungle Jim’s app. These can help with orientation; neither establishes a continuous accessible route or current aisle clearance.
quote: Store Map Your personal guide to the World of Food. Fairfield Eastgate
Explore the jungle on an interactive store map, unlock exclusive in-app deals, and more!

facts.text: Eastgate’s published store hours are daily 8 a.m.–10 p.m. Its holiday table lists Thanksgiving 8 a.m.–5 p.m., Christmas Eve 8 a.m.–6 p.m. and Christmas Day closed. The table has no year; confirm the intended holiday before travelling.
quote: Visit Eastgate
Open 7 days 8 AM to 10 PM
Thanksgiving 8:00 am - 5:00 pm Christmas Eve 8:00 am - 6:00 pm Christmas Day Closed

facts.text: For sandwich orders, Lehr’s invites customers to call 513-831-3411 ahead to reduce the wait. Confirm the collection point and any assistance needed; the page does not describe vehicle-side handoff.
quote: Alleviate your wait… Please call in your order. It will be ready when you are!

facts.text: The sandwich service is listed as Monday–Saturday 11 a.m.–5 p.m. and Sunday 11 a.m.–4 p.m.; these are sandwich-service hours, not the market’s full opening hours.
quote: Prime Sandwiches are served Mon. – Sat. 11 a.m. – 5 p.m. Sunday 11 a.m. – 4 p.m.

facts.text: The sandwich menu invites customers to ask about gluten-free bread options. This does not establish ingredients, cross-contact controls or suitability for a particular allergy.
quote: Ask about Gluten Free Bread options

facts.text: For Thanksgiving 2026, orders can be placed in person, by phone at 513-831-3411 or through the linked online ordering page. The posted online deadline is November 19 at 11:59 p.m.; later walk-ins depend on item availability.
quote: Place your order in person, on the phone (513-831-3411), or click the link to place online.
Online ordering closes Thursday, November 19th at 11:59 PM.
Walk-ins are welcome after the ordering deadline, with items subject to availability.
Thanksgiving 2026 Pick-Up:

facts.text: The published Thanksgiving 2026 pickup windows are November 23 and 24, 9 a.m.–7 p.m., and November 25, 9 a.m.–5 p.m. They do not establish a curbside collection procedure.
quote: Thanksgiving 2026 Pick-Up: Monday, November 23rd — 9am–7pm Tuesday, November 24th — 9am–7pm Wednesday, November 25th — 9am–5pm

facts.text: The Find Us page lists Monday–Saturday 10 a.m.–5 p.m., closed Sunday, and 513-683-5993 for contact before a visit.
quote: Hours Monday–Saturday 10:00 AM–5:00 PM Sunday - CLOSED

facts.text: For party orders, the market recommends requesting at least a week ahead and no later than three days before the event to help ensure availability. It warns that summer and holidays can be busy; inquiries are by phone at 513-683-5993.
quote: To ensure product availability, we recommend submitting your request at least one week and no later than three days before your party. Summer months and holidays can be particularly busy.
For inquiries, call 513-683-5993 .

facts.text: The Heat-N-Serve page asks customers to discuss allergy information with the team and lists allergens for individual dishes. Confirm the particular item and preparation arrangements before ordering.
quote: Please ask our team about allergy information
Lobster Bisque Creamy, smooth texture, sweet lobster flavor Contains shellfish, gluten, dairy

facts.text: The low-country-boil section describes a do-it-yourself kit ordered by phone; its FAQ says the market cannot cook that kit for customers. This limit is specific to the kit, not every prepared food sold here.
quote: DIY LOW COUNTRY BOIL
STEP 3: Call us to create your kit!
Can you cook it for me? Unfortunately No.

facts.text: The pantry says guests remain in their vehicles while volunteers load the food. This describes food loading, not assistance with moving or transferring a person.
quote: Guests remain in their vehicles while volunteers load their food.

facts.text: The pantry says it welcomes people beyond Boone County and requires neither an appointment nor documentation.
quote: You do not have to be a Boone County resident—everyone is welcome, and no appointment or documentation is necessary.

facts.text: The regular pantry session is the second Saturday of each month, 9–11 a.m. Check with the organizer for changes before travelling.
quote: The pantry is open on the second Saturday of every month from 9:00–11:00 AM.

facts.text: The pantry is a partnership of Christ’s Chapel and Immanuel Methodist Church. Christ’s Chapel’s page gives 3819 Turfway Road in Erlanger and 859-371-3787 as its contact location and phone.
quote: The Boone County Drive-Thru Food Pantry is a partnership between Christ’s Chapel and Immanuel Methodist Church
3819 Turfway Rd, Erlanger, KY, 41018, United States

address_quote: 3819 Turfway Rd, Erlanger, KY, 41018, United States

facts.text: The pantry serves Kenton, Boone, Campbell, Grant and Pendleton counties and applies a household-income eligibility scale. Confirm the current income limit with the pantry; the displayed table has no stated effective year.
quote: Our service area is Kenton, Boone, Campbell, Grant & Pendleton counties
We use the USDA Food Program Income Eligibility Scale

facts.text: For a first visit, the pantry asks eligible households to bring two items showing the applicant’s name and current address, plus identification for every household member. Examples include mail, bills or a driver’s licence for address evidence and school ID, a medical card or a birth certificate for household identification.
quote: If you fall within these two guidelines, then please bring the following items with you on your first visit:
Two pieces of ID with your name and current address (mail, bills, driver’s license, etc.)
ID for all members of your household (SS card, medical card, birth certificate, school ID, etc.)

facts.text: The first-visit instructions ask newcomers to arrive by 11:30 a.m. to allow registration before noon. Because the same page also lists evening sessions without first-visit instructions for them, confirm evening registration by phone.
quote: Please plan to arrive at our office no later than 11:30 if it is your first visit.
It will take several minutes to get you set up and into our system and we like to allow our volunteers to go home at noon.
First and Third Monday of the Month from 6:00-7:00 pm

facts.text: Published service hours are Monday–Friday 9 a.m.–noon and the first and third Monday evenings of the month, 6–7 p.m., with closure on major holidays.
quote: Service Hours (closed on all major holidays) Monday through Friday from 9am to noon First and Third Monday of the Month from 6:00-7:00 pm

facts.text: In bad weather, the pantry asks visitors to call 859-261-3649 for an updated recording if it is closed.
quote: In case of bad weather, please call our office (859-261-3649) for a recording which will be updated if we are closed because of bad weather.

facts.text: The contact page places the pantry at 4375 Boron Drive in Covington and gives 859-261-3649 for visit questions.
quote: Action Ministries 4375 Boron Dr Covington, KY, 41015

facts.text: The 2025 annual report describes monthly grocery deliveries by three local churches to some residents of The Colony, Hathaway Court and Arcadia who could not drive to the pantry. It says the deliveries could not include everything available at the pantry. This is historical, residence-specific information; current operation, enrolment and eligibility need confirmation.
quote: 2025 Overview of Action Ministries, Inc. December 31, 2025
Three local churches deliver groceries each month to about one hundred of the residents at The Colony, Hathaway Court and Arcadia who are unable to drive to Action Ministries to pick up groceries.
While we cannot take everything we have at the Mission to them because of logistics, we try to take the most useful items.

address_quote: Action Ministries 4375 Boron Dr Covington, KY, 41015
